thread:
incident-bot: Paging: p99 spike and streaming stalls observed on inference path -> customers reporting degraded streaming responses and tail latency > 10s. Auto-alert triggered by p99-slo-monitor.

oncall-mike: I’m on it, grabbing keys and will start triage. @sre-alyssa you seeing the same dashboards?

sre-alyssa: yep - control-plane auth latencies up, config-fetch p95 jumped to ~800ms in last 2m. Streaming tails spiking at p99 ~11.2s.

eng-raj: logs show a flurry of 429s from config-service to model-router, and tokenstore queries backing up. suspect rate-window enforcement causing retries.

support-lee: have two customers reporting timeouts during streaming (IDs: cust-673, cust-901). They're seeing partial tokens then stall. Customer impact likely medium->high.

incident-bot: Incident severity: S2 (multiple customers, degraded streaming). Notified oncall rotation and started incident timeline.

oncall-mike: Quick mitigation checklist: 1) open canary fallback to lower-capacity model, 2) increase control-plane auth token cache TTL, 3) temporarily relax config-service rate windows. Which is safest to do first?

eng-raj: I can flip the fallback route for streaming to model-serve-v1-fallback (lower cost but compatible) — no deploy, just routing change. Doing now: `curl -X POST https://console.internal/routing/override -d '{"route":"fallback","reason":"live mitigation"}'`

sre-alyssa: I'll raise token cache TTL in flight. Patch: `redis.set("auth:ttl", 300)` — applying to the controlplane cache cluster.

db-nora: DB p99 is elevated during bursts because of many small config fetches. We have heavy contention on the `feature_flag` table indexes. Suggest enabling read-through cache on the control-plane side as an immediate relief.

support-lee: noted, I'm sending a templated message to the affected customers: "We're investigating increased streaming latency; mitigation in progress. We'll update within 15m."

eng-raj: Routing change applied. Starting a smoke test against streaming endpoint.

eng-raj: smoke test results: streaming begins to flow through fallback but token throughput still struggling for some long-lived sessions. Partial improvement: p95 down from 2.1s -> 1.3s, p99 still ~7s.

sre-alyssa: TTL increase propagated to 3 of 4 control-plane nodes; one failed to pick up due to config sync issue. Pushing sync now.

incident-bot: oncall handoff scheduled in 25m. Current assignees: oncall-mike (primary), eng-raj (engineer), sre-alyssa (sre).

db-nora: rolling patch to enable read-through cache on config-service in progress. Command:
```
kubectl patch deployment config-fetch -n controlplane --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"config-fetch","env":[{"name":"READ_THROUGH_CACHE","value":"true"}]}]}}}}'
```

sre-alyssa: After cache enabled, we saw immediate reduction in DB read QPS by ~38%. p99 for config-fetch dropped to ~320ms.

support-lee: Customer update sent: "We've implemented a mitigation and are seeing partial improvement. Some sessions may still experience interruptions — next update in 15m."

product-sam: Any impact on feature flag rollouts? We need to ensure we don't accidentally roll back an important flag during mitigation.

eng-raj: Good point — I added a traffic rule to ignore feature-flag writes and only cache reads for now. No rollouts will be affected.

oncall-mike: Observability notes: collecting a few traces for streaming stalls and will attach to the incident. If p99 stays above 5s for another 10m we escalate to S1.

sre-alyssa: Noticed an auth-service retry storm from a subset of clients that fail early with 401 -> full reauth floods tokenstore. I’m applying a short-term client-backoff policy in the control-plane proxy: `max_retries=2, backoff_base=200ms`.

db-nora: We're also bumping DB connection pool max for tokenstore from 150 -> 300 to drain backlog, watching for CPU.

eng-raj: After retries/backoff + cache + routing fallback, streaming p99 is currently 2.9s and trending down. Tail stalls reduced significantly, long-lived sessions still a bit noisy.

support-lee: I received confirmation from cust-673 that streaming resumed and partial messages are coming through. They are still seeing occasional 5s spikes.

incident-bot: Customer impact summary: ~4% of streaming requests affected during peak (partial token emission then stall). No complete data loss reported.

oncall-mike: Handoff note for next oncall: maintain routing fallback, keep read-through cache enabled, monitor tokenstore connection pool, and coordinate with DB team for index tuning on feature_flag table.

product-sam: Requesting an evaluation window to run controlled flag reads against the cache to ensure consistency for 24h before making it permanent.

eng-raj: I'll create a short-lived canary to validate cache freshness: `curl -sS https://internal/config-cache/validate?key=feature_flag:beta_ui` and compare hashes.

sre-alyssa: Logging additional traces to S3 for postmortem. Action items captured in thread.

db-nora: Follow-up DB work: add a covering index on `feature_flag(namespace, name)` and audit slow queries; will schedule maintenance window if needed.

support-lee: I've queued a support follow-up with customers affected and will update after next status.

oncall-mike: Current state: mitigations in place, p99 reduced to acceptable levels (below 3s), customer impact decreasing. Transitioning to monitoring/retrospective. If anything regresses, ping this thread or page oncall.

incident-bot: Incident timeline saved; incident will be transitioned to postmortem triage in 24h.

eng-raj: quick note: config-service metrics to add to dashboards: `config.fetch.latency.p99`, `tokenstore.connections`, `featureflag.read_hits`.

sre-alyssa: tagging for postmortem: `controlplane-deps`, `streaming-tail`, `db-contention`.

oncall-mike: thanks everyone — handing off to next oncall shortly.

support-lee: final customer update going out now with mitigation summary and expected followups.

product-sam: filing a tracking ticket to review feature-flag read patterns and durable caching strategy.

incident-bot: Closing live mitigation. Postmortem owner assigned: eng-raj.
